pages.text: "Mom, I want to go into the wheat field!" Little brother Mumu hopped by the field. Mom said, "If you lose me, stop right there. All right?" Big sister Dodo's long legs held her head above the wheat.
Inside was yellow everywhere, with rustling wheat above Mumu's head. Then a grasshopper popped up before his nose! "Grasshopper!" Mumu turned quickly to follow.
Hop, hop went the grasshopper. Mumu stopped and twisted to look back. No Mom, no Dodo. Only yellow wheat all around. His heart pounded, and tears filled his eyes.
Then he remembered Mom's words. "Lose me, stop right there." Mumu planted both feet. Eyes shut tight, he took a big breath. "I won't run. I'll wait for Mom here."
Standing still, he looked up. Above the wheat rose a long neck! Mom! The longest neck at the mill looked this way and that for Mumu. "Mumu! Where are you?"
Right there, Mumu raised both wings and shouted hard. "Mom! I'm here!" He waited without running. The long neck turned his way. Wheat rustled apart.

Mom came through the wheat, Dodo waddling after her. Mom hugged Mumu warmly with a wing. "You stopped and called. Well done!" Her tail feathers swished beside him. "From now on, hold Mom's tail tight!"
Mumu held her tail feathers firmly with a wing. When Mom moved, he followed through the rustling wheat. Dodo watched him from the back. One tail flick. The yellow field wasn't scary now.
They left the field in one line. Mom first, Mumu middle, Dodo last. "One, hold Mom's tail tight! Two, lose her, stop still! Three, call Mom and wait!" Mumu called, "Hold Mom's tail tight!"
Back in the yard, Mom hugged Mumu firmly with a wing and patted his back. "You were so brave!" Even lost, stop and call, and Mom comes. Mumu smiled. "Hold Mom's tail tight!"
